note: Projectile presets for the fictional range. Mass and diameter are the published
nominal figures for each cartridge's bullet. Reference area is not stored: it is
derived from diameter as pi*d^2/4, so the two can never disagree.
The solver applies a SINGLE constant drag coefficient and does not model the Mach
dependence of real drag. Each drag_coefficient below is therefore a representative
value chosen so the constant-Cd trajectory matches the published remaining velocity
at the stated reference distance. It is accurate near that band and increasingly
wrong outside it, especially through the transonic region.
Cd is derived from the closed-form solution of the drag-only horizontal case,
v(x) = v0*exp(-k*x) with k = rho*Cd*A/(2m), giving Cd = 2*m*ln(v0/vx)/(rho*A*x).
reference_speed_mps is the published remaining velocity at reference_distance_m,
recorded so each coefficient can be re-derived and checked.

presets.name: 5.56x45 NATO, 62 gr
presets.description: Light, fast, sheds velocity quickly past 500 m.

presets.name: .308 Match, 175 gr
presets.description: Boat-tail match bullet; goes transonic near 900 m.

presets.name: 6.5 Creedmoor, 140 gr
presets.description: High sectional density for its calibre; low wind drift.

presets.name: .338 Lapua Magnum, 250 gr
presets.description: Very low drag; stays supersonic well beyond 1200 m.

presets.name: .50 BMG, 660 gr
presets.description: Heavy anti-materiel ball; enormous retained energy.

presets.name: 9x19mm, 115 gr
presets.description: Subsonic round-nose; drops sharply past 100 m.

presets.name: .45 ACP, 230 gr
presets.description: Heavy and slow; a very curved trajectory.

presets.name: .22 LR, 40 gr
presets.description: Light subsonic rimfire; useful for short-range practice.

presets.name: Lead round ball, 17.5 mm
presets.description: Smooth sphere. Above the classic 0.47 because 300 m/s is transonic, where sphere drag rises sharply.

presets.name: Steel sphere, 10 mm
presets.description: Low sectional density; decelerates very quickly. Near the classic 0.47 subsonic sphere value.
